title: Derive real push and pull-request change sets in shadow mode
goal: Derive a deterministic repository-relative change set from exact Git commit identities for both push and pull_request events, then emit the corresponding validation plan while the existing full kernel still runs.
inputs: verified E3 impact and validation-plan engine
outputs: shadow plan from GitHub event commit range
invariants: Git refs are data arguments and never shell-expanded as commands
unknown change evidence escalates rather than skips
full legacy kernel remains authoritative until adaptive execution parity is proven
security_properties: commit identities are validated before git use
selected executor keys remain closed and built-in
no arbitrary command execution from manifests or plan JSON
acceptance_tests: unit test proves additions, deletions and both sides of a rename reach the change set
push and pull_request workflows execute real git-changes plus validation-plan before the full kernel

performance_budget.rationale: CI adaptation exists to reduce repeated validation cost
metrics: change-set derivation should be negligible compared with validation execution
adaptive runner must not run checks outside the selected prerequisite-closed plan

rollback.strategy: revert adaptive CI integration and restore full legacy kernel execution

definition_of_done: change-set command validates full commit IDs
deleted and renamed paths are represented safely
push and pull_request workflow events provide exact base/head commits
shadow validation-plan uses the real change set
full kernel remains unchanged as the authoritative gate during this sublot
